title: The cache directives
summary: Which directive keeps the bytes off the disk, which one only makes a cache ask first, and what a hard reload is really sending.

sources.author: web.dev
sources.title: Prevent unnecessary network requests with the HTTP Cache

cards.front: Which of `no-store` and `no-cache` keeps the response off the disk, and what does the other one do instead?
cards.back: `no-store`: a cache must not store any part of the request or the response. `no-cache` stores it and revalidates before each reuse, so a copy on disk is expected.

cards.front: `no-cache` and `max-age=0`. What is the difference, and which one used to be spelled as the other?
cards.back: `max-age=0` is stale on arrival; `no-cache` may never be reused without asking first. `no-cache` was once written `max-age=0, must-revalidate`, which MDN calls "a remnant".

cards.front: The dashboard is personalised. Which directive keeps it out of a shared cache, and does that keep it off the laptop?
cards.back: `private`, and no: it narrows storage to the browser, so the copy still lands on disk. Keeping it off this machine takes `no-store`.

cards.front: You shipped `no-store` and the old value keeps coming back. What did the header not do?
cards.back: Evict: `no-store` stops a response being written and says nothing about one already stored. A new URL gets past it.

cards.front: A hashed bundle, the HTML that names it, and a bank statement. One `Cache-Control` line each.
cards.back: `public, max-age=31536000, immutable`, then `no-cache`, then `no-store`. The asset's name changes when its bytes do, so it can never be wrong.

cards.front: What does `no-store` on every response cost you, and what does MDN recommend as the default instead?
cards.back: The 304 that would have cost nothing, so the hashed bundle downloads again on every navigation. MDN recommends `no-cache` with `private` instead.

cards.front: A reload and a hard reload. What does the browser send for each, and which one can come back as a 304?
cards.back: A reload sends `Cache-Control: max-age=0` with `If-None-Match` and `If-Modified-Since`, so it can come back 304. A hard reload sends `no-cache` and no conditions, so it gets a 200. That is Chrome, Edge and Firefox; Safari differs.

cards.front: "It works when I hard reload." What has that told you, and why does it not close the ticket?
cards.back: That the stale copy was above the network line. It is not a fix, because only you sent `Cache-Control: no-cache`, for one navigation in one browser.
